status: drafted via direct read-through of the real extracted Geneva 1560 verse text (Assets/Resources/Verses/Geneva/genesis_1.json, all 50 chapters), cross-checked tier-naming style against the existing KJV Genesis.json but built independently from the Geneva text itself
notes: Content/structural verdict: this Geneva Genesis is narratively IDENTICAL to the familiar 50-chapter/Protestant-canon Genesis — same episodes in the same chapter order (Creation, Fall, Cain and Habel, the Flood, Babel, the patriarchs Abraham/Izhak/Iaakob, the Joseph novella) — so the KJV Genesis.json's 19-manager-tier shape was a valid starting template, not force-fit; every tier below was independently re-verified against the real Geneva verse text, not copied blind. The real differences are orthographic (Elizabethan/Geneva spelling, predating and diverging from the 1611 KJV's own spelling choices in ~50 years' worth of small ways) plus a handful of genuinely Geneva-specific proper-noun quirks: 'Iaakob' (Jacob), 'Izhak' (Isaac), 'Ioseph' (Joseph), 'Iudah' (Judah), 'Beniamin' (Benjamin), 'Rahel' (Rachel), 'Kain'/'Habel'/'Sheth' (Cain/Abel/Seth), 'Heuah' (Eve, Gen 3:20), 'Henoch' (both the Cainite city-namesake AND the 'walked with God' patriarch — Geneva spells them identically, same collision KJV has as 'Enoch'), 'Enosh' (KJV 'Enos'), 'Kenan' (KJV 'Cainan'), 'Iered' (KJV 'Jared'), 'Methushelah'/'Methushael'/'Mehuiael' (KJV Methuselah/Methusael/Mehujael), 'Melchi-zedek King of Shalem' (Gen 14:18 — Geneva spells the city 'Shalem', not 'Salem'), 'Iehouah-ijreh' (Gen 22:14), 'Zaphnath-paaneah' and 'Poti-pherah' (Joseph's Egyptian name and his father-in-law, Gen 41:45). REAL NAMING-COLLISION FOUND, Geneva-specific and worth flagging distinctly from the KJV file: Geneva spells BOTH the pre-Flood patriarch in Shem's line (Arpachshad's son, Eber's father, Gen 10:24/11:14-15) AND Judah's third son (Gen 38:5) as 'Shelah' — KJV disambiguates these two men by spelling the elder one 'Salah', but Geneva uses the identical spelling for both; flagged here with distinct ids (shelah_ancestor_geneva / shelah_iudahson_geneva) so they are never conflated. Minor textual quirk, not a new character: Gen 31:53 spells Nahor's name 'Nabor' once ('The God of Abraham, and the God of Nabor...') where every other occurrence in this same text is 'Nahor' — treated as an internal Geneva print/spelling inconsistency, not a distinct person. All other naming collisions already known from the KJV pass carry over unchanged since the underlying people/events are the same: two Henochs (as above), two Lamechs (Kain's line, Gen 4:18-24, vs Noah's father, Gen 5:28-31 — both 'Lamech' in Geneva too), two Nahors (Serug's son/Terah's father vs Terah's son/Abram's brother — both 'Nahor', see the 'Nabor' quirk above), and Potiphar (captain of Pharaoh's guard who buys Ioseph, Gen 37:36/39:1) vs Poti-pherah (priest of On, Ioseph's father-in-law, Gen 41:45) — two distinct men the text itself keeps separate by spelling, not a collision to resolve.
